content.summary: The existing acceptance checks child creation, while the completed 24EC50 live tree reaches only depth one. Add an end-to-end grandchild test for both schedulers and rerun the full regression after P8 finishes. Preserve live depth as an observed limit and do not spend additional model calls to manufacture a deeper tree.
findings: The baseline child-creation assertion is insufficient for a multi-level execution claim. The required new observation is an actual depth-two node produced by the engine, not a manually assembled tree or a scheduler-only probe.

Three distinct initial roots and four investigation rounds require the scheduler to descend after initial-root exploration. Synthetic threshold values deliberately isolate traversal from natural-language proposal quality.
Keep the existing three-call per-root limit. The fourth refinement exhausts its selected root, so a fourth reconstruction must not occur; the new grandchild must remain in the unresolved frontier.

Require correct parent/root lineage, counted calls, generated Java checks, retained unresolved state and a verified report for both BFS and UCT. No traversal-order or efficiency ranking is a promotion criterion.
Do not change acceptance inputs during P8. Append P9 after its immutable result, then review the exact new source digest. A failing focused test requires diagnosis and repair before full acceptance.
This is engineering evidence only. The live examples remain development sources; deeper synthetic execution does not establish completeness or correct English interpretation.
